about: A deterministic shuffle, and the two ways one stops being a control.
THE FIRST is the closed form that cancels the salt:
looks salted, but salt + salt*i is salt*(i+1), which is zero modulo i+1.
The salt cancels identically, so sixty-four draws are ONE permutation drawn
sixty-four times. `varies` is the case that catches it.
THE SECOND is the position-only rule, live until this vector existed:
does not cancel, but j depends only on the position and the salt — never on
the data, never on a stream. Both call sites passed salt = 3, so there was
exactly one null corpus, ever. And j collapses to 0 whenever i+1 divides 14.
`degenerate` is that case, stated as the thing a shuffle must not be.
AND THE LIMIT, which is not a bug in the shuffle but in what it is asked to
falsify: a permutation preserves the multiset exactly, so it cannot falsify
any claim that is a function of the multiset alone — a floor, a ceiling, a
congruence, a concentration. Finding the law again on shuffled values is
evidence the null was wrong, not that the law is false. `blind` pins the
three quantities that survive, so a miner can refuse to build a control that
